He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]], with whom he won an [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA national championship]] in 2019. He also won an NBA championship with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]]. ==Early life== Diakite was born in [[Conakry]], [[Guinea]] to Aboubacar Sidiki Diakite and Aminata Kaba and was raised as a Muslim.{{cite web |title=Mamadi Diakite |url=https://virginiasports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=251 |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |access-date=March 30, 2019}}{{cite web |last=Needelman |first=Josh |title=Grabbing the fruit: Virginia forward Mamadi Diakite works to put the ball back in Guinea's hands |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/grabbing-the-fruit-virginia-forward-mamadi-diakite-works-to-put/article_4f7ebabc-6f07-5b1e-87e5-0339e844ab68.html |website=[[The Daily Progress]] |access-date=March 30, 2019 |date=March 12, 2019}} His father was the health inspector general of Guinea and his mother was an [[Obstetrics|obstetrician]].{{cite web |last=Doughty |first=Doug |title=Cavs in waiting game for Blue Ridge School big man Diakite |url=https://www.roanoke.com/sports/uva-insider-cavs-in-waiting-game-for-blue-ridge-school/article_f21eb752-9777-5259-b447-1808293405a5.html |website=[[The Roanoke Times]] |access-date=March 30, 2019 |date=September 11, 2014}} Diakite grew up playing [[association football|soccer]] in streets and parks but later started playing basketball because of his height and athleticism.{{cite web |last=Newman |first=Caroline |title=A Tale of Two Mamadis |url=https://news.virginia.edu/content/tale-two-mamadis-how-these-uva-basketball-stars-forged-brotherhood |publisher=[[University of Virginia]] |access-date=March 30, 2019 |date=March 6, 2018}}{{cite web |last=Zamoff |first=Zach |title='Keep digging': Mamadi Diakite's journey to basketball success |url=http://www.cavalierdaily.com/article/2019/01/keep-digging-mamadi-diakites-journey-to-basketball-success |website=[[The Cavalier Daily]] |access-date=March 30, 2019 |date=January 23, 2019}} Due to the lack of basketball opportunities in Guinea, he tried to draw attention from the United States through [[Facebook]]. As a result, Diakite was contacted by Hassan Fofana, a Guinea native and former college basketball player, and with his help joined [[Blue Ridge School]], a [[boarding school]] in [[Saint George, Virginia]]. ==High school career== Diakite enrolled at Blue Ridge School in early 2014.{{cite web |last=Dillman |first=Damon |title=Diakite Expected to Enroll at UVa This Fall |url=https://www.cbs19news.com/sports/headlines/Diakite-Expected-to-Enroll-at-UVa-This-Fall-320806291.html |publisher=[[WCAV]] |access-date=March 30, 2019 |date=August 5, 2015 |archive-date=April 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401164558/https://www.cbs19news.com/sports/headlines/Diakite-Expected-to-Enroll-at-UVa-This-Fall-320806291.html |url-status=dead }} When he first came to the United States, he could only speak French, and Guinean former basketball player Mamadi Diane was among those who helped him acclimate. Diakite played two basketball seasons at Blue Ridge School and also earned [[varsity letter]]s in [[track and field]] and soccer, because the school required students to play a sport each season.{{cite web |last=Reid |first=Whitey |title=Blue Ridge's Diakite draws interest from big-name schools, including UVa |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/blue-ridge-s-diakite-draws-interest-from-big-name-schools/article_c45d7eda-53eb-11e4-9859-001a4bcf6878.html |website=[[The Daily Progress]] |access-date=March 30, 2019 |date=October 14, 2014}} As a senior in basketball, he averaged 12 points, eight rebounds, and four blocks per game while leading his team to the Virginia Independent Schools Athletic Association (VISAA) Division II state title and a Virginia Independent Conference (VIC) championship. Diakite was named second-team All-VIC in soccer in 2014–15, and he won back-to-back VIC [[high jump]] titles. In basketball, he was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the top prospect in the state of Virginia. On August 4, 2015, Diakite committed to play for [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], turning down offers from several other [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] and [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].{{cite web |title=Mamadi Diakite, Blue Ridge School, Power Forward |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Mamadi-Diakite-75982/high-school-136035/ |access-date=March 30, 2019 |publisher=[[247Sports]]}}{{cite web |title=Mamadi Diakite - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/204446 |access-date=March 30, 2019 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} ==College career== [[File:Mamadi Diakite (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Diakite at [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].]] After committing to Virginia, Diakite [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the class of 2015 and [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first college basketball season with Virginia, hoping to physically prepare for college basketball and adjust to the college lifestyle during 2015–16.{{cite web |last=Wood |first=Norm |title=Highly recruited forward Mamadi Diakite commits to Virginia, may reclassify to 2015 |url=https://www.dailypress.com/sports/colleges/acc-all-access-blog/dp-spt-highlyrecruited-forward-mamadi-diakite-commits-to-virginia-may-reclassify-to-2015-according-to-repor-20150804-post.html |website=[[Daily Press (Virginia)|Daily Press]] |access-date=March 31, 2019 |date=August 4, 2015 |archive-date=April 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401164525/https://www.dailypress.com/sports/colleges/acc-all-access-blog/dp-spt-highlyrecruited-forward-mamadi-diakite-commits-to-virginia-may-reclassify-to-2015-according-to-repor-20150804-post.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |last=Kelly |first=Ryan M. |title=Diakite officially joins Virginia basketball program |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/diakite-officially-joins-virginia-basketball-program/article_0d30d3ae-5293-11e5-9faa-87f697a71fb7.html |website=[[The Daily Progress]] |access-date=March 31, 2019 |date=September 3, 2015}} He debuted as a redshirt freshman on November 15, 2016, recording eight points and four rebounds in a 72–32 win over [[2016–17 St. Francis Brooklyn Terriers men's basketball team|St. Francis Brooklyn]].{{cite web |title=No. 8 UVA Routs St. Francis, 72-32 |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2016/11/15/No_8_UVA_Routs_St_Francis_72_32.aspx |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |access-date=March 31, 2019 |date=November 15, 2016}} On December 6, Diakite scored a season-high 12 points in a 76–53 victory over [[2016–17 East Carolina Pirates men's basketball team|East Carolina]].{{cite web |title=Post Game Notes |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2016/12/6/Post_Game_Notes.aspx |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |access-date=March 31, 2019 |date=December 6, 2016}} Through 32 games in the season, he averaged 3.8 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Mamadi Diakite NCAA Men's Basketball Stats |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/3947156/type/mens-college-basketball |access-date=January 14, 2024 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} As a redshirt sophomore on November 23, 2017, Diakite matched his career high in scoring, with 12 points and five rebounds in a 68–42 win over [[2017–18 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] at the [[NIT Season Tip-Off]].{{cite web |title=Virginia Game Notes vs. Vanderbilt |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2017/11/23/Virginia_Game_Notes_vs_Vanderbilt.aspx |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |access-date=March 31, 2019 |date=November 23, 2017}}{{cite web |title=UVA Handles Vanderbilt in NIT Tip-Off, 68-42 |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2017/11/23/UVA_Handles_Vanderbilt_in_NIT_Tip_Off_68_42.aspx |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |access-date=March 31, 2019 |date=November 23, 2017}} On February 3, 2018, he chipped in 12 points for a second time, in a 59–44 victory over [[2017–18 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]].{{cite web |title=Hunter, Guy lead No. 2 Virginia over Syracuse, 59-44 |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2018/2/3/Hunter_Guy_lead_No_2_Virginia_over_Syracuse_59_44.aspx |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |access-date=March 31, 2019 |date=February 3, 2018}} Through 34 games, Diakite averaged 5.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 0.5 blocks per game. In the third game of his 2018–19 redshirt junior season, he recorded a career-high 18 points on November 16, in a 97–40 win over [[2018–19 Coppin State Eagles men's basketball team|Coppin State]].{{cite web |title=Hot-Shooting Hoos Top Coppin State |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2018/11/16/mens-basketball-hot-shooting-hoos-top-coppin-state.aspx |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |access-date=March 31, 2019 |date=November 16, 2018}} Diakite matched his career high on January 9, 2019, posting 18 points, seven rebounds, and two blocks in an 83–56 victory over [[2018–19 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]].{{cite web |title=No. 4 Virginia Nabs 83-56 ACC Road Win at Boston College |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2019/1/9/mens-basketball-no-4-virginia-nabs-83-56-acc-road-win-at-boston-college.aspx |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |access-date=April 1, 2019 |date=January 9, 2019}} On March 30, in the [[Elite Eight]] round of the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]], he recorded 14 points, seven rebounds and four blocks in an 80–75 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] win over third-seeded [[2018–19 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]].{{cite web |last=Joseph |first=Andrew |title=Carsen Edwards and Mamadi Diakite shared incredible moment of sportsmanship before OT |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2019/03/carsen-edwards-mamadi-diakite-purdue-virginia-sportsmanship-elite-eight |publisher=For The Win |access-date=April 1, 2019 |date=March 31, 2019}} Diakite made a buzzer-beating shot to send the game to overtime.{{cite web |title=Virginia Advances to Final Four |url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2019/3/30/mens-basketball-virginia-advances-to-final-four.aspx |publisher=University of Virginia Athletics |access-date=April 1, 2019 |date=March 31, 2019 |archive-date=March 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331131232/https://virginiasports.com/news/2019/3/30/mens-basketball-virginia-advances-to-final-four.aspx |url-status=dead }} In the [[Final Four]], they played [[2018–19 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]]. Diakite grabbed 6 rebounds and played a total of 36 minutes, but had only 2 points on 25% shooting. Virginia won the game 63–62 after teammate [[Kyle Guy]] made 3 free throws.{{Cite web |date=April 7, 2019 |title=Guy hits 3 FTs with 0.6 left, Virginia shocks Auburn 63-62 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401123375 |access-date=January 14, 2024 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} In the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 national championship]], they played [[2018–19 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]]. Diakite had 9 points on 50% shooting, and grabbed 7 rebounds in 25 minutes of playing time.{{Cite web |date=April 9, 2019 |title=Virginia 85-77 Texas Tech (Apr 8, 2019) Box Score - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401123374 |access-date=January 14, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}} [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] won the game in overtime 85–77, giving Virginia its first-ever national championship. He dyed his hair blonde in late February 2019 then kept that essential look for the remainder of his college career.{{Cite web |date=March 31, 2019 |title=Mamadi Diakite Nationality, Ethnicity, & Background |url=https://heavy.com/sports/2019/03/mamadi-diakite-nationality-ethnicity-background/ |website=heavy.com}} He declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] after winning the national championship but withdrew his name from the draft before the withdrawal deadline date to return to Virginia for his last season of eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Horne |first=Chris |date=May 29, 2019 |title=Mamadi Diakite Withdraws From 2019 NBA Draft, Will Return To UVA |url=https://virginia.sportswar.com/article/2019/05/29/mamadi-diakite-withdraws-nba-draft-will-return-uva/ |access-date=January 14, 2024 |website=virginia.sportswar.com}} Diakite set a new career high of 19 points to go with 13 rebounds in a 65–34 win against [[2019–20 James Madison Dukes men's basketball team|James Madison]] on November 10, 2019.{{cite news |title=Diakite has 19 points and 13 rebounds for No. 11 Virginia |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168171 |access-date=November 20, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 10, 2019}} He matched his career high of 19 points on November 19, helping the Cavaliers defeat [[2019–20 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]] 61–55.{{cite news |title=Diakite, No. 7 Virginia hold off Vermont, 61-55 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168197 |access-date=November 20, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 19, 2019}} Diakite set a new career high of 21 points in a 70–59 loss to [[2019–20 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]] on December 22.{{cite news |title=Bolden leads South Carolina past No. 9 Virginia, 70-59 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168276 |access-date=March 9, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 22, 2019}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Diakite was selected to the Second Team All-ACC.{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/8/athlete-awards-2020-acc-mens-basketball-award-winners-announced.aspx|title=2020 ACC Men's Basketball Award Winners Announced|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=March 9, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2020–2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Diakite signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on November 24, 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-jaylen-adams-and-mamadi-diakite-two-way-contracts|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Jaylen Adams And Mamadi Diakite To Two-Way Contracts|date=November 24, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 21, 2021}}{{cite web|last=Oakes|first=Jamie|title=Mamadi Diakite signed by the Milwaukee Bucks|url=https://247sports.com/college/virginia/Article/2020-NBA-Draft-Milwaukee-Bucks-sign-Mamadi-Diakite-to-two-way-contract-UVA-Basketball-Virginia-Cavaliers-155199895/|website=247 Sports|date=November 21, 2020|access-date=November 22, 2020}} When the [[Wisconsin Herd]] made the decision to not play the 2020–21 season, Diakite was sent to the [[Lakeland Magic]] to fulfill the G League part of his contract,{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/milwaukee-bucks-forward-mamadi-diakite-transferred-to-lakeland-magic/n-5664933|title=Milwaukee Bucks Forward Mamadi Diakite Transferred to Lakeland Magic|date=February 5, 2021|website=OurSportsCentral.com|access-date=April 21, 2021}} making his debut for Lakeland on February 11, 2021.{{cite web |date=February 11, 2021 |title=02/11/21: Austin Spurs @ Lakeland Magic |url=https://gleague.nba.com/games/20210211/auslak/ |access-date=April 21, 2021 |website=NBA.com |archive-date=April 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421215233/https://gleague.nba.com/games/20210211/auslak/ |url-status=dead }} He appeared in 12 games with Lakeland while averaging 18.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, 2.1 blocks and 2.1 assists in 27.7 minutes and was named to the [[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League First Team]], the NBA G League All-Defensive Team and the NBA G League All-Rookie Team en route to the G League title with Lakeland. On April 21, 2021, Diakite signed a multi-year standard NBA contract after making 11 appearances with the Bucks. He won the NBA championship in his rookie season with the Bucks.{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Mamadi Diakite To Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-mamadi-diakite-multi-year-contract|website=NBA.com|date=April 21, 2021|access-date=April 21, 2021}} On September 24, he was waived by Milwaukee.{{cite web|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Bucks waive Mamadi Diakite|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bucks-waive-mamadi-diakite/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=September 25, 2021|access-date=September 25, 2021}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2022)=== On September 26, 2021, Diakite was claimed off waivers by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|title=Thunder Claims Mamadi Diakite|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/release/diakite-210926|website=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2021|access-date=September 27, 2021}} However, he was waived on October 16.{{cite web|title=Thunder Waives Diakite, Jaworski and Sarr|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder-waives-211016|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021}} On January 11, 2022, Diakite signed a 10-day agreement with the Thunder.{{Cite web|date=January 11, 2022|title=OKC Thunder news: Thunder signs Mamadi Diakite to 10-day hardship deal|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2022/01/11/okc-thunder-news-thunder-signs-mamadi-diakite-to-10-day-hardship-deal/|access-date=January 11, 2022|website=OKC Thunder Wire|language=en-US}} Diakite signed a second 10-day contract on January 21.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-diakite-220121|website=NBA.com|title=Thunder Signs Mamadi Diakite to 10-Day Contract|date=January 21, 2022|access-date=January 21, 2022}} He signed a third 10-day contract with the Thunder on January 31.{{cite web |title=Thunder Signs Mamadi Diakite to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-diakite-220131 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 31, 2022 |date=January 31, 2022}} On February 9, he was released by the team, in order to open up a roster spot for [[KZ Okpala]], acquired in a trade with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires KZ Okpala and Amends Conditions of First Round Pick|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-okpala-220209|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2022|access-date=February 9, 2022}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2022–2023)=== On September 26, 2022, Diakite signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |date=September 26, 2022 |title=Cavaliers Add Four to Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-22-training-camp-roster-220926 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA}} He was waived on October 15,{{Cite web |date=October 15, 2022 |title=Cavaliers Waive Five Players |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-player-waiving-221015 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} but was re-signed to a two-way contract by the team two days later.{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2022 |title=Cavaliers Sign Mamadi Diakite to a Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/cavaliers-sign-mamadi-diakite-to-a-two-way |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA}} He would end up playing in 22 games, starting in two. In the first game where he started against [[NBA MVP]] [[Joel Embiid]], he held the superstar to just 19 points, 6 rebounds, 6 assists, and 37.5% from the field. He also drained 2 three-pointers during the matchup. In his second start of the season, Diakite was matched up against the [[New York Knicks]] where he recorded 2 rebounds and a block. While most of the time he was traveling with the G League affiliate, he never missed out on too much. ===Westchester Knicks (2023)=== On October 19, 2023, Diakite signed with the [[New York Knicks]],{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks sign Mamadi Diakite and Brandon Goodwin|number=1715114425311490426|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 19, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}} but was waived two days later.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Mamadi Diakite, Brandon Goodwin, Isaiah Roby and Duane Washington Jr.|number=1715832489313182178|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}} On November 9, 2023, Diakite was named to the opening-night roster for the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2023-24 Official Roster|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2023-24-official-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2023|access-date=December 3, 2023}} ===San Antonio / Austin Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-mamadi-diakite-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 1, 2024|access-date=January 3, 2024}} and on March 2, he was waived by the Spurs.{{cite tweet|first=Tom|last=Orsborn|title=#Spurs make the following moves reported earlier official: 1, They've converted Barlow’s two-way deal to a standard NBA contract; 2, They've signed RaiQuan Gray and Jamaree Bouyea to two-way deals; 3, They've waived forward Mamadi Diakite.|number=1764032846534959265|user=tom_orsborn|date=March 2, 2024|access-date=March 2, 2024}} ===Return to Westchester / New York Knicks (2024)=== On March 6, 2024, Diakite returned to the [[Westchester Knicks]]{{cite tweet|author=Westchester Knicks|title=Welcome back, Mamadi‼️|number=1765430611139817619|user=wcknicks|date=March 6, 2024|access-date=March 7, 2024}} and on March 14, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Mamadi Diakite to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-sign-mamadi-diakite-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 14, 2024|access-date=March 14, 2024}} On March 25, he
